subagent_summary: With the incumbent hint 2/8 public rollouts scored 1; the six failures all committed early to one reading of the public number, found that reading self-contradictory for a single private value, and then either looped to the token cap (3 of 8 hit the length limit) or emitted a guessed divisor. The revision makes the sum-vs-product role an explicit hidden coordinate of the candidate state and adds the rule that a branch dies only when it fails for every private value, which is exactly the step the wrong rollouts skipped.

All 8 training rollouts were correct, so the incumbent's weakness is transfer (heldout 0.125), not this question: it prescribes the problem-specific substitution w=(z-1)/z and a Mobius image argument rather than a portable rule. The successful rollouts all converged only after reducing to a modulus condition |z-1|=2|z| and completing the square, while the longest ones burned 8k-12.5k tokens enumerating the six roots and fitting a circle through sampled points, hitting self-contradictions; none named the Apollonius circle. One rollout nearly rejected the circle because |z| was not constant, so the revision moves modulus-first to step one, names the Apollonius/perpendicular-bisector dichotomy, and warns that a non-origin-centered circle has varying |z|.

All 8 rollouts framed union = 5 - overlap correctly, but 6 of 6 failures ended with finish_reason=length at the 16384-token cap and the 2 successes only barely finished (~15.5-15.9k tokens), so the failure mode is budget exhaustion, not a wrong setup. The incumbent hint's instruction to parameterize the angle and minimize a piecewise triangle/sector expression drove exactly that: failures looped over trial angles and tangency guesses (30+ 'but how' restarts each, repeated 'too complex to visualize') and never reached a closing computation. The revision replaces the open-ended minimization with a decisive invariance test at the k-fold symmetry center plus an explicit stop condition, which is the step both winners stumbled onto only after heavy flailing.

All 8 public rollouts scored 0 (three ran out of tokens). Every one applied the equal-spacing condition to adjacent board entries, which may come from different polynomials, derived the vacuous contradiction 'a degree-5 polynomial would have to be constant', then guessed a small number (2, 5, 6, 10) or declared the count unbounded. None ever partitioned the indices by which polynomial was chosen, so the per-polynomial root bound and the multiply-by-family-size step never happened; the revised hint forbids the adjacent-difference move explicitly and spells out the grouping, non-degeneracy, product bound, and tightness construction.

7/8 public rollouts were correct; the single failure ran out of tokens after inverting the argument-ratio direction when converting the y-difference of two base-1/2 logs, which produced a negative discriminant. It then spent thousands of tokens re-verifying identical algebra and finally guessed, so the hint now names the base<1 direction trap, adds a cheap ratio sanity-check on the known points, and converts 'no real/in-domain root' into a signal to flip the sign/branch assumption once rather than loop.

All 8 training rollouts scored 0. Five concluded the delivery order is deterministically reversed (answering 1 and 0), and three instead assumed every item is equally likely to be last (answering 1/4), with several also treating the last item delivered as the bottom of the pile rather than the top. The incumbent hint's abstract state-graph advice did not stop these; the revision names the stack push/pop model, states the bottom/top orientation rule, and explicitly rejects both the forced-outcome and equiprobable-path fallacies while keeping the forced-move probability-1 weighting.

All 8 rollouts (0/8) collapsed the same way: they set P(x)=sum a_i x^i and read the rows as P(k)=0, swapping node with exponent, then burned the budget hunting a spurious extra root or chasing the x-coefficient of a Vandermonde product (six hit the 16384-token cap; one concluded a_1=0, another 1/2005). The revised hint forbids that role swap, states explicitly that the unconstrained constant term is why L(p) reads off the top coefficient, and gives a one-node test-polynomial recipe plus a small-case check so the same technique transfers to any moment/weight system.

All 8 public rollouts scored reward 1 (train_i = 1.0), so the training question is saturated and the only headroom is transfer, where the incumbent scores just 9/80. The incumbent's phrasing is bound to this item's surface features ('equal-street layout', 'every listed stage total', 'maximum-feasible-count interpretation'), and rollouts spent long stretches re-litigating that undefined jargon (4-15 restatements plus 6-23 'wait' backtracks each, up to 6928 tokens), so it reads as item-specific scaffolding rather than portable method. I replaced it with the same underlying procedure stated generically - name the hidden count, derive it from integrality/gcd plus structural grouping constraints, state the tie-break assumption, then aggregate-scale-divide and sanity-check - which should carry to unseen problems of this class.

All 8 rollouts scored 0 and 7 of 8 hit the 16384-token cap: every one set up p=ax^3+bx^2+cx-24, q=ex^3+fx^2+gx+30 and tried to match all ten coefficients of the degree-9 composition, then looped on self-contradictions (a^2=a, 3a^2=0) it could not resolve. The incumbent hint gestured vaguely at 'a shared affine coordinate' but never told the student what that coordinate is, so nobody tried a centered ansatz; the revision names the common-fixed-point substitution, gives the leading-coefficient consequence that forces the odd-degree sign flip, and says to recover the center by adding the two supplied values.

Only 2/8 rollouts were correct and five of the six failures hit the token cap while trying to derive an abstract bitwise/affine formula for the composed permutation, exactly what the incumbent hint asks for first. The failures that did terminate asserted cycle structures they never traced (order 2 for the size-4 case, a bogus odd-length cycle for size 8), so the revision front-loads concrete tabulation of one full operation plus an explicit disjoint-cycle lcm step and defers any symbolic formula.
